group.name: Domain-Specific Foundation Model Pretraining
group.definition: 의료·생명과학·농업·로봇·시계열처럼 데이터 형식과 제약이 서로 다른 영역에서, 과제별로 따로 모델을 학습해야 하는 문제를 대규모 사전학습과 재사용 가능한 표현 학습으로 해결하는 기술이다. 실제 구현에서는 여러 데이터셋과 모달리티를 정렬하고, 구조·시간·공간·생물학적 사전지식을 반영한 사전학습을 수행한 뒤 zero-shot, in-context learning, fine-tuning 또는 도메인 적응으로 새로운 과제와 환경에 적용한다. leaf_005가 확률적 동역학의 생성·시뮬레이션과 제어를 중심으로 한다면, 이 그룹은 주로 다양한 downstream task에 재사용할 표현과 예측 backbone을 만드는 데 초점을 둔다.
group.evidence_summary: 여러 멤버에서 기존의 과제별·데이터셋별 모델 대신 대규모 사전학습 모델을 만들고, 이를 다양한 downstream task와 환경으로 이전하려는 공통 방향이 반복된다. 데이터 대상은 EHR와 시계열부터 single-cell·spatial omics, 병리 이미지, 로봇 행동, 농업 영상까지 넓지만, 핵심 해결 방식은 이질적인 입력에서 재사용 가능한 표현을 학습하는 것이다. 멀티모달 정렬, 구조화 데이터 처리, cross-subject·cross-device·cross-platform 일반화, zero-shot 또는 few-shot 적응이 공통적인 기술 문제로 나타난다. 따라서 하나의 응용 분야라기보다 도메인 특화 데이터에 foundation model 패러다임을 적용하는 기술군으로 묶인다.
group.why_emerging: 대규모 유전체·단일세포·공간 데이터, 병원 수준 임상 데이터, 웨어러블 생체신호, 로봇 상호작용 데이터처럼 서로 다른 형식의 데이터가 빠르게 축적되고 있다. 그러나 라벨은 제한적이고, 장비·조직·지역·로봇 embodiment가 바뀌면 기존 과제별 모델의 성능을 그대로 이전하기 어렵다. 이 때문에 여러 데이터셋과 모달리티에서 공통 표현을 학습한 뒤 적은 라벨이나 추가 학습으로 새 조건에 맞추는 구조가 필요해진다. 동시에 프라이버시, 불규칙 샘플링, 공간 구조, 생물학적 사전지식처럼 범용 언어·비전 모델만으로 처리하기 어려운 제약이 도메인 특화 사전학습의 필요성을 높인다.

sources.title: 2nd ICML Workshop on Foundation Models for Structured Data

claims.name: Foundation Models for Tabular and Time-Series Data
claims.evidence: Over the past two years, predictive foundation models tailored to structured data have emerged, enabling in-context learning and transfer across heterogeneous datasets and schemas, challenging the traditional “train per dataset” paradigm.

claims.name: Multimodal Structured Foundation Models
claims.evidence: We also explicitly encourage submissions that study scaling across datasets, model size, and compute; and multimodality for structured foundation models (e.g., image-tabular modeling in medical diagnosis; text-time-series modeling for ECG interpretation). While these directions have driven transformative progress in text and vision, they remain largely underexplored for tabular and time-series data.

sources.title: ICML 2026 3rd Workshop on Multi-modal Foundation Models and Large Language Models  for Life Sciences

claims.name: Multi-modal Foundation Models for Biological Data
claims.evidence: To address these limitations, there is a growing need for multi-modal foundation models and LLMs that can effectively integrate and reason over diverse biological modalities.

claims.name: Multi-omics Representation Learning
claims.evidence: Multi-modal foundation models for learning joint representations of multi-omics data.

sources.title: 1st AAAI Workshop on SPARTA — Spatial Reasoning and Therapeutics with AI : From Omics to Imaging

claims.name: Spatial Multi-omics Integration
claims.evidence: Spatial multi-omics integration (combining spatial transcriptomics and proteomics) for target identification.

sources.title: 1st ICLR Workshop on Time Series in the Age of Large Models

claims.name: Time Series Foundation Models
claims.evidence: The organizers bring extensive research experience and proven leadership in the time series foundation models domain, with diverse backgrounds from industry and academia. Collectively, we have led advances on 3 key dimensions: foundational model development– creating some of the first time series foundation models including Lag-Llama, Chronos, Moment, Moirai, and TimesFM, advanced applications– establishing initial frameworks for reasoning and agents in time series through MLZero and TimeSeriesGym, and rigorous evaluation and benchmarking using tools such as Context-is-Key, GIFT-Eval, TimeSeriesExam, and fev-bench.

sources.title: 8th Robot Learning Workshop:  Is Physical AI Going Zero-Shot?

claims.name: Foundation Models for Robotics
claims.evidence: The year 2025 has seen an unprecedented acceleration in the scale and diversity of foundation models for robotics, with the trend continuing in 2026.

sources.title: AI at Scale for Clinical Impact: Cancer Pathology Foundation Models

claims.name: Clinical-Scale Pathology Foundation Models
claims.evidence: ASCI is a NeurIPS 2026 workshop in Sydney, Australia for researchers, clinicians, and industry teams building cancer AI models that can move from technical benchmarks to validated clinical impact.

sources.title: ai_index_report_2026

claims.name: Scientific Foundation Models
claims.evidence: 원문: "A 111-million-parameter protein language model, MSAPairformer, beat previous leading methods on ProteinGym, and a 200-million-parameter genomics model, GPN-Star, outperformed a model nearly 200 times larger." 이유: 상대적으로 작은 과학 특화 모델이 기존 선도 방법과 훨씬 큰 모델을 능가한 사례로, Scientific Foundation Models의 구조 혁신과 도메인 특화 연구가 확장될 근거를 제공한다.

sources.title: First International Workshop on Neuro for AI & AI for Neuro: Towards Multi-Modal Natural Intelligence

claims.name: Neuro-Inspired Multimodal Foundation Models
claims.evidence: Sessions highlighted how biologically grounded features derived from large-scale cell-type and connectivity datasets can inform transformer and graph-based models, enhancing their learning performance and energy efficiency.

sources.title: Generative AI in Genomics (Gen^2): Barriers and Frontiers

claims.name: Foundation Models for Functional Genomics
claims.evidence: With recent large-scale data initiatives launched to support GenAI models creating an inflection point for the field, timing is ideal.

sources.title: ICML 2026 Workshop on Structured Data for Health

claims.name: Foundation Models for Clinical Structured Data
claims.evidence: While recent advances in foundation models, multimodal learning, and large language models offer new opportunities to unify these data sources, the health domain presents unique constraints—including privacy, interpretability, irregular sampling, and clinical deployment—that remain largely underexplored.

claims.name: Structured Probabilistic Inference for Foundation Models
claims.evidence: Similar to last year, we also encourage submissions that explore the relevance of probabilistic inference in the era of foundation models.

claims.name: Foundation Models for Single-Cell and Transcriptomic Biology
claims.evidence: Building towards such a system begins with learning meaningful representations within individual modalities, which form the foundations for scaling the complex heterogeneous biological signals into a coherent model of a cell, and combining them into integrative models that capture biology’s complexity.

sources.title: Machine Learning for Genomics Explorations (MLGenX)

claims.name: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Foundation Models
claims.evidence: STAGE: A Foundation Model for Spatial Transcriptomics Analysis via Graph Embeddings with Hierarchical Prototypes

sources.title: mckinsey_tech_trends_2026

claims.name: Scientific Foundation Models
claims.evidence: These are large-scale AI models and deep learning surrogates trained on scientific data—including molecules, proteins, biological sequences, materials structures, and scientific literature—that can generate predictions, insights, and designs across scientific domains. 이 문장은 Scientific Foundation Models의 학습 데이터와 연구 활용 범위를 직접 정의한다.

sources.title: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop on Foundation Models for the Brain and Body

claims.name: Foundation Models for Biosignals
claims.evidence: This growing wealth of data is driving a shift toward foundation models: large-scale, pretrained AI systems designed to learn from biosignals and generalize across diverse downstream applications, from brain-computer interfacing to health monitoring.

sources.title: NeurIPS 2026 Workshop: Foundation Models for Temporal Systems  From Forecasting to World Modeling

claims.name: Temporal Foundation Models
claims.evidence: Temporal machine learning is moving beyond task-specific prediction. The next challenge is to build foundation models that can forecast, simulate, adapt, and support decisions in systems that evolve across time, modalities, and scales.

sources.title: NeurIPS Workshop on Machine Learning for Spatially Resolved High-dimensional Biology

claims.name: Spatially-Aware Multimodal Foundation Models
claims.evidence: The first spatial and tissue-aware foundation models have appeared in the past two years, and computational pathology has started to combine histology with molecular measurements.

sources.title: RoboPAD: Post-Training Adaptation of Robot Foundation Models

claims.name: Robot Foundation Models
claims.evidence: Pretrained robot foundation models are increasingly capable, yet real-world deployment still requires adaptation to new environments, embodiments, tasks, and failures.

sources.title: The 2nd Workshop on Foundation Models for Science: Real-World Impact and Science-First Design

claims.name: Scientific Foundation Models
claims.evidence: We argue that foundation models for science must be built differently from language and vision. Scientific data are physical, causal, spatiotemporal, and often scarce or biased; objectives must reflect mechanistic fidelity, not just predictive accuracy.

sources.title: The First International Workshop on AI in Agriculture

claims.name: Foundation Models for Agriculture
claims.evidence: Generative AI, foundation models, and transfer learning for agriculture
